propositions: Pass-1 context-limit escalation returns bare Anthropic model ids instead of preserving the provider qualifier from the run's configured model when no model-class table is configured.

The _rung_target function compares rung provider inference against rung class resolution without considering the actual run model, causing provider-qualified primaries like bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0 to degrade to bare claude-opus-4-8.

When cfg.model is provider-qualified through cfg.model_provider and escalation substitutes a bare model id, the resulting composed id (e.g. bedrock:claude-opus-4-8) is invalid for the provider, causing hard failure or unbudgeted cross-provider spend.
The one-criterion retry on entry rung frontier executes with bare model id substitution before deep escalation is needed, affecting common retry paths not just rare deep-escalation cases.

The fix makes _rung_target thread the primary run model and apply provider-agreement logic: preserve the target if providers agree or either is undeterminable; return primary verbatim on the primary's own rung; drop higher rungs that cross providers when the class table is unconfigured.
